newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan urges G7 to help solve Lima siege.
newsitem.headline: Japan urges G7 to help solve Lima siege.

text.p: Japan on Friday called for the Group of Seven (G-7) industrialised nations to intervene to help solve the Lima hostage crisis, saying Tokyo was in touch with other members of the club of rich nations on how to do so.

Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda told a news conference Japan had already begun discussions with other G7 members -- Britain, German, Italy, France, Canada and the United States -- to seek an end to the 10-day-old drama.
Ikeda said the summit of G7 leaders in Lyon, France, in July approved a list of 25 practical measures to defeat terrorism.

The package included pledges to reinforce police cooperation and training, to share intelligence, make extradition procedures easier, cut off sources of terrorist funding and weapons, and strengthen national anti-terrorism legislation.

"It is clear that the international community should not condone terrorism. It is also necessary for the international community to act as one to help resolve this crisis by setting free all the hostages peacefully, and at an early date," Ikeda said. "With this in mind, we have already started consultations (with the other G7 member states)."
